description: Self-referential binding is inserted verbatim, not re-expanded (single-pass, CONFORMANCE_SPEC.md 2.2.3 rule 1). The inner 'x' survives; nothing loops.
Mutually-referential bindings {a -> b, b -> a} are a simultaneous SWAP, not a cycle: each variable of the INPUT is replaced once.
Chained bindings {a -> b, b -> c} are NOT transitive: 'a' becomes 'b', never 'c'. This is what makes a binding map usable as a rename map.
A variable appearing REPEATEDLY is not a cycle: every occurrence in the input is substituted, at every sibling position.
A self-referential binding under an operator node carrying metadata: the replacement is inserted verbatim and 'wrt' is preserved unchanged.
